doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Working with Rosie Clooney in California
summary: Miller takes Conniff west; only the Rosie Clooney session happens, and he praises her nervous warmth and perfect pitch.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah, they copied it from that, yeah. And then yeah, that was used again in that. And anyway, and then I did the Marty Robbins stuff, “White Sport Coat.” So Mitch — you asked about the deal. Mitch said, at a meeting, he said, “hey everything this Conniff guy’s doing is getting on the charts,” you know. And so he was going out to the west coast, and he said, “I won’t be using you for a couple of weeks, I’m going out to the west coast, and I’m going to do Doris Day, Rosie Clooney and Jo Stafford.” And I said, “Oh, why don’t you take me with you?” And he says, “You wanna go with me?” And I says, “Yeah, I’d like to go with you.” He said, “I’ll tell you what. You pay your own plane fare, I’ll give you all three artists, you do four charts for each artist,” that would be twelve charts I’d do, and I was getting I think $150 an arrangement. And I said, “Good, you’ve got a deal.” So I went out with him and we got out there and it turned out one of the artists, I forget who it was, was I guess it was Jo Stafford got what I’ve got today, kind of a laryngitis thing and couldn’t sing. I lost her. Doris Day got into a contractual dispute and decided not to record right then. So all I did was the Rosie Clooney, four sides. And she was great to work with, I thought she was terrific. When I walked in the studio she says, “You’re Ray Conniff?” I said, “Yeah.” “The arranger?” I says, “Yeah.” She says, “You’ve got to help me.” And she grabbed ahold of me and hugged me. And her little body, she was very small then, her little body was just shaking she was so nervous. I says, “Rosie, you’re Rosie Clooney, aren’t you?” And she says, “Yeah.” I says, “You are great, what are you worried about? You are such a great success.” She is one of the greatest musicians I’ve ever worked with. And she sang a note, bing, it was right on the button. I mean she didn’t scoop up to the note, she really hit them right in tune and stayed in tune, and a great sound. So she was wonderful. So she relaxed and she sang great. But
